plan-tests-files-one-planner-per-story: Judgment issue about the project's own shipped tooling: the fix is the owner's choice of how /plan-tests divides stories among planner tasks. Route question, not upstream: this repo is the ok suite's source, and the canonical skill at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/ is project-owned; the vendored copy at .claude/skills/plan-tests/ is suite-owned and /ok regenerates it from that source.

Evidence, re-verified (the filed problem still holds):
- plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/SKILL.md:42 (step 5.1): "File one story task per story under `.ok-planner/design/stories/`: `tasks file --role story --prompt story --agent ok-opus --key <slug> --brief \"story <slug>; ...\"`". It files one per story on every run, whatever the window's status; the window (step 3, SKILL.md:30) already lists the stories changed and the files changed since the stamp, and step 5 does not use it to narrow the planners.
- plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md:84: "The task prompt for a story planner, one task per story." The prompt (core.md:88-120) reads one story whole, its recorded scenarios, the window's diffs, every sprint closed since the stamp, the last run's results, and then "the code that carries the story" from its entry points. Every planner repeats the window and sprint reads, and stories that share code read it once each.
- Items are keyed by story slug (core.md:147-148, `--key <slug> --field source=story:<slug>`), and SKILL.md:45, :58, :66, :70 refile "the planner" a failure or review finding names; "the latest done task of each planner stands, and its items replace the earlier task's."

Mechanism: planning cost is one fresh ok-opus agent per story, each paying the shared reads (window, closed sprints, results file) plus its own code reading, so cost grows linearly with the story count. The filer's numbers: linescout at v28.0.0, 107 stories, 107 story planners plus one runtime planner, 13.29M of 14.22M planning tokens.

Corpus: scenario-list-decided-once says "Planners read each story, the code that carries it, and what changed since the stamp, and sort every recorded scenario"; it is silent on how many stories one planner takes. tests-check-scenarios bounds scenarios ("Each story way yields at most one scenario per program") and is silent on planner division. No story or decision commits to one planner per story, so no corpus change is forced by any option; the change edits SKILL.md step 5 and the story planner prompt in core.md (and, for batching, the --key/source mapping and the refile rule).

Harm: cost only; no accept-list entry covers it, and none needs to, since this is a judgment issue.

Options, each with its main cost:
- A. Batch by shared code, up to a set size. Cost: a grouping pass must read the code (or the story annotations) before planning; a refile for one story's failure re-plans its whole batch unless the refile rule changes to per-story refile within a batch.
- B. Batch by count, N stories per task in catalog order. Cost: unrelated stories share a context, so per-story code reading is not saved, only the shared reads; same refile cost as A.
- C. Keep one per story and accept the cost. Cost: planning cost keeps growing with the story count.
- D (filer missed): on a window whose status is not `new`, file planners only for the stories the window touches (stories changed, stories whose recorded scenarios' tests reach changed files, stories cited by changed code), and carry the rest forward unchanged; plan every story only on `new`. Cost: no saving on a first plan (the linescout run), and a story whose carrying code changed without a citation or a recorded test can be missed. Combines with A or B.
- E (filer missed): batch by citation, grouping stories whose @story: annotations sit in the same files, which gives A's grouping from a grep instead of a code reading. Cost: reach ends where annotations end; un-annotated stories fall back to B or C.
No stated rule decides among these.

Siblings to rule with: drain-loop-wakes-the-session-on-every-agent-return (the same 107 returns wake the session), plan-tests-asks-the-owner-after-the-planners-run, plan-tests-cannot-widen-an-approved-plan, plan-tests-offers-retire-on-a-first-plan (same story planner prompt), test-write-tasks-chain-on-shared-support-files.

body: plan-tests-cannot-widen-an-approved-plan: Judgment issue about the project's own tooling; the fix lies in the canonical /plan-tests source this repo owns (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/SKILL.md and core.md, plus scripts/tests for a new mode), so route question. Evidence, re-verified: SKILL.md:30 (step 3) still stops on a current window: "Where the status is `current`, say that the tests stand where the last test sprint left them, and stop." scripts/tests:window_entry (lines 292-325) sets status `current` only when no file changed since the stamp and no test file is unclaimed; any changed file makes it `reached`. SKILL.md:42 (step 5.1) files one story planner per story whenever the window is reached, not only for changed stories. The story planner's table, core.md:124, already says "Code supports a way the story gives its benefit, and no scenario covers it. | `new`", so a planner on any reached window may add scenarios; what it lacks is any instruction to read the earlier plan's calls. Calls live only in records: scripts/tests:531-532 builds plan["calls"] into the -plan.json beside the test sprint, and test-state.json keeps no calls. One filed claim is slightly off: planners do not "refile every recorded scenario" by rule only; they sort each recorded scenario (core.md:118). Mechanism: (1) a quiet tree never opens a window, so widening waits on an unrelated change; (2) a planner reading earlier calls reads a record, which decision:records-stay-out-of-context allows only where "a skill ... reads a record it names", so the skill would have to name the earlier plan file. Corpus: decision:scenario-list-decided-once: "Planners read each story, the code that carries it, and what changed since the stamp, and sort every recorded scenario" and "The stamp ... opens the next window"; it is silent on reopening a story with no change. decision:tests-check-scenarios: "Each story way yields at most one scenario per program that carries it" bounds how far widening can go. Harm: none an accept-list entry covers; it is tooling scope. Options: A (widen mode taking stories or every story with left-out calls) costs a second entry path and a decision:scenario-list-decided-once delta naming it; B (every story planner reads its earlier calls) costs nothing new on a reached window but nothing on a current one, and needs the skill to name the earlier plan record; C (owner names stories, window treats them as changed) needs a way past the `current` stop and leaves finding thin stories to the owner; a missed option D: let /plan-tests run on a `current` window when the owner names stories, combined with B, so the left-out calls are read and the owner need not hunt. No stated rule decides among them. Siblings to rule with: plan-tests-caps-each-story-way-at-one-scenario-per-program (the cap is a large part of why the plan was thin), plan-tests-files-one-planner-per-story.

drain-loop-wakes-the-session-on-every-agent-return: Judgment issue about the project's own tooling; the drain loop and tracker are canonical sources this repo owns (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_tasks/drain.md, scripts/tasks), so route question. Evidence, re-verified: drain.md:24 "After that the window slides, one in for one out: when an agent returns, stamp its task's usage, call `next`, and where it lists a task waiting, start exactly one fresh agent of that task's profile, never more than one per return." scripts/tasks:format_instruction (tasks:599) prints `tasks=` followed by every waiting task id joined by commas, so a run with 400 issued tasks prints 400 ids per call. The ids serve one check, drain.md:24: "Where `next` lists a task that as many agents as tasks were started for and no agent claimed, stop and report it". The filed facts hold. Mechanism: each return is a new model request that rereads the whole session context, and each adds a hand-back, a task notification, the `next` output, and any hook text, so cost per return grows with the run's length. Part of the measured growth (112,000 to 680,000 tokens before the first test) came from the planning session's own reads, not only the drain. Corpus: decision:no-execution-engine: "The suite ships a task tracker and a drain loop that every executor runs on ... Neither one plans, gates, or judges"; decision:subagent-model-follows-job: a pinned profile "may fork itself, and spawns nothing else", and every dispatch, "the Agent tool and every `agent()` call in a Workflow script", names its model; decision:team-execution-cold-gate: the run shares "one cached prefix per profile". Harm: no accept-list entry; it is cost. Options: A (background script dispatching agents) leaves the harness's Agent tool, so the subagent-model hook and the one-cached-prefix design no longer apply as written, and it edges toward the workflow engine decision:no-execution-engine rejects; B (counts not ids, one-line hand-backs, batched refills) stays inside every live decision, but the stuck-task check needs ids, so `next` would print ids only for a stuck task, and the session still wakes once per return; C (a coordinating agent per stage) contradicts decision:subagent-model-follows-job ("spawns nothing else") and needs a corpus change; a missed option D: run the drain inside a Workflow script, whose `agent()` calls the corpus already names, so the harness keeps dispatch and the session wakes when the workflow ends. A and D both change drain.md and decision:no-execution-engine's wording of who runs the loop. No stated rule decides among them. Siblings to rule with: test-write-tasks-chain-on-shared-support-files (same run's throughput), plan-tests-files-one-planner-per-story.

test-write-tasks-chain-on-shared-support-files: Judgment issue about the project's own tooling; the fix lies in scripts/tests and the plan-tests prompts this repo owns (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests, skills/plan-tests/core.md), so route question. Evidence, re-verified: scripts/tests:holders_of (969) maps each file of every open test or legacy task to its holder; scripts/tests:filed_after (978-983) sets `after` to the holder of each of the new task's files and makes the new task the holder of all of them; scripts/tests:stage_write (1003-1005) builds each write task's files as its test path, its old test path, and every support file the scenario names (plus legacy support entries). So any two scenarios naming one support file run in filing order, one at a time. core.md:140 asks a story planner to name "its support files"; core.md:393 tells the write task "You change test files only: the files your task's files name", so a task that needs a helper must hold the support file. The filed facts hold. Corpus: decision:team-execution-cold-gate: "two writers never hold one file at once, and readers run beside anything"; drain.md:24: "the caller filed the tasks so that no two ready at once hold one file, and readers run beside anything". decision:scenario-list-decided-once records "its support files" per scenario; decision:test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests: "A fix never changes a test, a support file, or a fixture". The corpus is silent on how test tasks share support. Harm: no accept-list entry; it is throughput. Options: A (support tasks first, test tasks read support without holding it) keeps one writer per file, and a test that finds support lacking has no file it may change, so it needs a call or a follow-up support task; B (several writers to one support file under the tracker's lock) contradicts "two writers never hold one file at once" in decision:team-execution-cold-gate and drain.md, so it needs a corpus change and a merge rule; C (one task per group sharing support) keeps the rule, at the cost of large tasks; a missed option D: planners split support into files a scenario reads and files it adds to, and only an add holds the file, so most tasks run beside each other and the few that add helpers chain. No stated rule decides among A, C, and D; B is ruled out by a live decision unless the owner changes it. Siblings to rule with: drain-loop-wakes-the-session-on-every-agent-return.

plan-tests-asks-the-owner-after-the-planners-run: Judgment issue about the project's own tooling; the fix lies in the canonical /plan-tests skill this repo owns (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/SKILL.md, core.md, and scripts/tests for an assembly check), so route question. Evidence, re-verified: SKILL.md:42 (step 5.1) files story planners with the brief "story <slug>; the last run is at <the results path, or none>" and the runtime planner with "the last run is at ...": no scope and no answer reach a brief. SKILL.md:47-54 (step 6) asks the owner only after the drain, from `tests plan --questions`. The runtime planner prompt (core.md:183-236) both plans runtime scenarios and finds the unguarded entry points in one task, so it can plan a runtime scenario for a program it also asks about; it reads the stamp's unguarded list (core.md:195), but a no-guard answer given in this session reaches no planner. No step asks the owner for scope at all; the planners pick test paths from the project's test paths and the tree. The filed facts hold. Corpus: decision:scenario-list-decided-once: "The owner decides each scenario whose outcome changed or whose code is gone, and each program no story serves, and approves the whole list once"; decision:tests-check-scenarios: "A program no story serves gets no test: the owner either asks a sprint for the story it serves or records it as unguarded". Both are silent on when the owner answers and on a planning scope. Harm: no accept-list entry; it is cost and a rerun. Options: A (ask scope and program questions first) needs the unguarded-program search split out of the runtime planner into a pass that runs before the planners, then every brief carries the answers; B (scope first only) is a prompt and brief change, and runtime planners may still plan for programs answered no-guard later; C (assembly refuses out-of-scope or unguarded scenarios) keeps a mechanical check but still spends the planner run; A and C combine. Outcome-changed questions can only come after a planner reads the window, so no option moves those first. No stated rule decides among them. Siblings to rule with: plan-tests-declares-the-runner-before-planning (both settle owner inputs before planning), plan-tests-fixes-a-finding-by-rebuilding-the-planner (the rerun cost), plan-tests-reviews-a-whole-plan-with-one-agent, tests-window-ignores-declared-folders (where test paths come from).

plan-tests-declares-the-runner-before-planning: Judgment issue about the project's own tooling; the fix lies in the canonical /plan-tests skill and tests tool this repo owns (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/SKILL.md, core.md, scripts/tests), so route question. Evidence, re-verified: SKILL.md:26 (step 2) proposes `testing.run` from how the project runs tests today and records it with `tests declare --run`, before any planner runs. scripts/tests:106 `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 600`; scripts/tests:254 reads `testing.get("timeout", DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)`; scripts/tests:811 kills a test at that timeout. `tests declare` takes `--timeout` (scripts/tests:29), but step 2 never offers it. The story planner reads `testing.run` only to know whether to name a test (core.md:139-140); the write task reads it at core.md:404 ("the command that runs one test, which your test must suit"), inside the unattended run. Steps 7-10 (SKILL.md:58-70) check no planned test against the runner or the timeout. The filed facts hold. Mechanism: the runner is fixed before the plan says what kinds of test it needs, and the first point that meets a mismatch is a write task under /goal, which has no owner to ask; the verify prompt (core.md:645) sends back "a longer timeout" as a hidden failure, so the fix loop cannot raise it either. Corpus: decision:scenario-list-decided-once: "The project declares how one test runs as `testing.run` in its configuration, a command holding `{path}` and, where the runner needs it, `{name}`" (one command); decision:test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests: "A test sprint runs unattended under `/goal`", and its alternatives reject "Stop at the first failing test and ask the owner: ... a test sprint never stops to ask". Harm: no accept-list entry covers the planning order; the run that stopped to ask departed from decision:test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests, which is a separate prompt question. Options: A (check after assembly, ask before approval) is a skill step plus a planner field naming each test's kind and setup, with one more approval question; B (one command and timeout per kind) changes the one-command commitment in decision:scenario-list-decided-once, so it needs a corpus delta and a config shape change in scripts/tests:testing; C (planners plan only what the runner runs, calls for the rest) leaves those ways untested, which decision:tests-check-scenarios would record as neither a scenario nor a gap; a missed option D: step 2 also asks the timeout, and the planner prompt tells planners the runner and timeout, with A's check as the backstop. No stated rule decides among them. Siblings to rule with: plan-tests-asks-the-owner-after-the-planners-run (both settle owner inputs before planning).

plan-tests-offers-retire-on-a-first-plan: Judgment issue about the project's own tooling; the fix lies in the canonical story planner prompt this repo owns (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md, {{TEST-STORY-PLANNER-PROMPT}}), so route question. Evidence, re-verified: core.md:123 still reads "| The story's text dropped the scenario. | `retire` |" with no limit to recorded scenarios. scripts/tests:check_plan refuses it, scripts/tests:619-620: `if action in ("keep", "retire") and sid not in old:` "%s names a scenario the stamp did not record". scripts/tests:stage_write (tests:1001) already skips a retire with no test and no old test, but assembly refuses first, so that branch never sees an unrecorded retire. SKILL.md:58 (step 7) answers a refusal by refiling the whole planner. The filed facts hold. Mechanism: on a first plan (window status `new`) no scenario is recorded, so every retire item fails assembly; the task tracker has no verb to drop one item. Corpus: decision:scenario-list-decided-once: "Planners ... sort every recorded scenario. The rules decide a scenario whose story dropped it", so retire is a sort of a recorded scenario; decision:test-sprints-own-the-tests and decision:tests-check-scenarios are silent on it. Harm: no accept-list entry; it is a wasted planner run. A stated rule decides the one compliant change: decision:scenario-list-decided-once makes retire a sort of a recorded scenario, and scripts/tests:check_plan already enforces that, so option A (qualify the row: retire applies only to a scenario the stamp recorded; a way the story dropped that no scenario recorded gets no item) aligns the prompt with the tool and the decision. Option B would turn a refusal into a silently absorbed item, which plumbline-coding rule 4.6 ("A caught error never ends in a bare log line or a silent default") argues against. The author may write a generated ruling for A. Siblings to rule with: task-tracker-cannot-drop-an-item, plan-tests-fixes-a-finding-by-rebuilding-the-planner, plan-tests-rejects-a-malformed-scenario-id-only-at-assembly (same class: a planner item the assembly refuses, fixed only by a whole rerun).
